utterances.speaker: JUDGE WEINBERG DE ROCA
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Madam Registrar, would you call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-98-30/1-A, the Prosecutor versus Miroslav Kvocka, Mladjo Radic, Zoran Zigic, and Dragoljub Prcac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WEINBERG DE ROCA
utterances.text: Thank you. The appearances, please. For the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. BRADY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Helen Brady appearing for the Prosecution, and with me today is Ms. Norul Rashid, and our case manager Ms. Lourdes Galicia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WEINBERG DE ROCA
utterances.text: Thank you. For the -- for Mr. Kvocka, I understand that Mr. Simic is on line. Mr. Simic, can you hear us?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can hear you. I hear you. Good afternoon, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WEINBERG DE ROCA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. For Mr. Radic, the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Zoran Jovanovic, attorney, and I appear together with Mr. Toma Fila who is absent today, but we are the Defence team of the accused Mladjo Radic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WEINBERG DE ROCA
utterances.text: For Mr. Zigic, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, good afternoon. My name is Slobodan Stojanovic, and I represent the Defence counsel for Mr. Zoran Zigic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WEINBERG DE ROCA
utterances.text: And for Mr. Prcac.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Jovan Simic, attorney, and I am Defence counsel for Mr. Dragoljub Prcac. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WEINBERG DE ROCA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I would like to know if the accused can understand the proceedings. Mr. Radic, please.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT RADIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WEINBERG DE ROCA
utterances.text: Mr. Zigic.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT ZIGIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WEINBERG DE ROCA
utterances.text: And Mr. Prcac.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT PRCAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WEINBERG DE ROCA
utterances.text: This is a Status Conference pursuant to Rule 65 bis. This morning, the Presiding Judge has signed two decisions, one decision on the new evidence, on the four motions pursuant to Rule 115, and one decision scheduling the hearings in this case. I understand the Prosecution received them a bit earlier and that the accused -- the Defence counsel present have only received them a few minutes ago and that Mr. Simic has yet not been served. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The Defence of Mr. Kvocka has still not received that material, but we expect to receive it shortly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WEINBERG DE ROCA
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Simic. Is there any questions the Defence counsel want to raise during the Status Conference?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your permission, Your Honour, on behalf of Mr. Zigic, regardless of the fact that the decision has been made with respect to the schedule and the Scheduling Order has in fact been received, we should like to raise two issues and to try to explain things. The first point is the disclosure of certain documents and material, and within the frameworks of disclosure there are a couple of problems. The first is that before this Tribunal there is an ongoing trial for other individuals for the same acts, and that that is being hidden from me and Mr. Zigic and from myself as his Defence counsel. Now, you will tell me that this is confidential material and data with respect to us. However, the indictment for those same acts and crimes against other individuals and also the accompanying material as an annex to the indictment exists; on the other hand, witnesses are being heard who testified against Mr. Zigic. They're being heard in other trials under pseudonyms that we are not aware of so that we cannot know how they testified about the same events that they testified in our trial. And the third point with respect to disclosure that I wanted to say, and I think the Prosecution could be of most help to us there, we have heard unofficially that in Prijedor some material has been seized by the security service. There is a lot of that material, and we assume that there is much in it which has to do with our indictment and the judgement. So I think that the OTP can be of great assistance there. So that was the first problem, disclosure with respect to certain material and facts. And the second problem was a question of payment. I must say that my presence at some of the scheduled court hearings will have to remain an open question because I have arrived here today at my own cost, as I have done several times in the past. For 18 months, I have received no payment for my work at all, and I feel that this will be a problem for me if I am to appear in future. It is a problem of my very existence. Not only do I have to pay my own expenses, but I have to leave the work that I do which provides me with a salary and income. I have to pay for my own accommodation, my own travel expenses, et cetera. Now, I didn't ask for a set salary, but it is very difficult for me to continue in this way because I have been doing this for 18 months. Mr. Zigic himself has said that he is indigent, that he doesn't have the means to pay me for my services. The legal aid service has told me that it is my duty to work as a Defence counsel regardless if I'm paid for my services or not. So if I can use a more humourous term and say that this is forced labour in a way, and I know that forced labour was a subject discussed in this court of law, but I don't know whether this coercion will be -- not only is it not paid, but the person providing the service is forced to pay for his own accommodation and travel expenses. So as I say, the question of my continued appearance in court remains open. It is of course my desire to help both the Tribunal and Mr. Zigic himself, however, under the present conditions, this is a very real problem that I have to contend with. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WEINBERG DE ROCA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Does the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Prosecution want to respond to the aspect of disclosure?

utterances.speaker: MS. BRADY
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Your Honour. The Prosecution at present is up-to-date in its review for Rule 68. We have conducted the searches of our evidence collection up until the end of 2003, and last week, the 10th of February, we disclosed a further two documents to the appellants which came out of that review. Mr. Stojanovic mentioned the related trials, and I assume he's meaning by that the case of Meakic and others and the Brdjanin case. Your Honour, our searches encompass ongoing trials, and as we discover any material, we, in accordance with our continuing obligations to disclose, do provide this material to the appellants, so there can be no question of hidden evidence in these matters. In terms of Mr. Stojanovic's submission relating to -- that he heard that there had been material seized in Prijedor, Your Honours, I'm not in a position to speak directly on that at this point. I can say that if the material has now entered into our evidence collection, this would also have been covered by our searches. But to be on the safe side, of course, after this Status Conference I can make some inquiries to make certain that our searches have included this material and will of course do the necessary reviews and provide it to the appellants, if any, as soon as we can. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WEINBERG DE ROCA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Before responding to Mr. Stojanovic, I would like to know if other Defence counsel want to raise any question now.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. We have become acquainted with the contents of the decisions and rulings with respect to the motion for additional evidence with respect to Mr. Radic. The proposal was refused, so as far as Radic's team goes, up to the 23rd of March we have nothing to add. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WEINBERG DE ROCA
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no questions, Your Honour, and I don't want to broach any new subjects because we have been given the ruling that we have been waiting for such a long time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WEINBERG DE ROCA
utterances.text: Thank you very much, then. What I would suggest to the Defence counsel of Mr. Zigic is that with regard to disclosure, he should seek access to the Trial Chamber under Rule 75(J) to ask for access of such evidence or material as he deems necessary. With respect to the second motion, it is the intention of the Bench to make a decision on Mr. Zigic's appeal against the decision of the Registry regarding the payment of the fees of Defence counsel, but this is nothing which can be decided within the framework of a Status Conference. Mr. Simic, would you like to add something?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would have something to say with respect to Rule 115.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WEINBERG DE ROCA
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Or, rather, I do not have -- I have nothing to bring up at this point. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WEINBERG DE ROCA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. BRADY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. If I can just raise two points. Firstly, the Prosecution is reviewing the decision of this morning concerning the 115 decision, and if we have any difficulties in meeting the 27 February deadline for the filing of rebuttal, we will let you know immediately. At this point, we don't anticipate any difficulties in light of the nature -- the two witnesses have been admitted, but if we have any difficulties in meeting that deadline, we'll let you know as soon as possible. The second --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WEINBERG DE ROCA
utterances.text: Just let me add that I very much hope that you have no problem meeting the deadline.

utterances.speaker: MS. BRADY
utterances.text: We hope so too, Your Honour. And the second point is that, as I mentioned, we disclosed last week on February the 10th two further documents to the appellants, and in light of the hearing schedule and the fact that the hearing will be on the 23rd of March, the appellants may like to place on the record now or at some point close in the future as to whether they will be filing any further 115 motions as a result of that recent disclosure or on the basis of any other material, just in light of the fact that we're moving now towards a certain deadline. That would be very helpful. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WEINBERG DE ROCA
utterances.text: Thank you very much, but I'm sure counsel for the Defence will let us know if they intend to file something additional. I think then that this Status Conference can be adjourned.
